items.title: Verstappen tops final practice; top five fit inside 0.274s
items.summary: The official 22-car FP3 classification has Max Verstappen first in 1:11.622, 0.025s ahead of Kimi Antonelli; Lando Norris is third at +0.131s, George Russell fourth at +0.184s and Charles Leclerc fifth at +0.274s. FIA Document 36 separately deletes listed FP3 lap times for Rafael Camara at Turn 1 and Verstappen at Turn 4; it does not replace the classification. Formula1.com reports Hamilton's session ended early after vibration and smoke reports, and rain arrived at the finish. Race Director Document 38 allows all teams to close their garage doors due to anticipated severe weather; it does not announce a session delay.
items.why_it_matters: The top five are tightly grouped, but this is a single practice session rather than a qualifying order. Verstappen's 30-place penalty and the decision's conditional grid allocation make the official starting order important.

items.title: FIA confirms Ferrari pair's 10-place drops and Verstappen's 30-place ruling
items.summary: The Stewards' Documents 35 and 37 impose 10-place drops for Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, respectively, after each receives a fifth ICE. Document 33 separately imposes a 30-place drop on Max Verstappen for his fifth ICE, turbocharger and exhaust. Document 39 imposes a 30-place drop on Sergio Perez for his fifth ICE, fifth turbocharger and fourth MGU-K. If either driver is classified in Qualifying, the respective decision allocates his Race-grid position under Article B2.5.4.b.iv. Perez's fifth PU-ANC in Document 30 is within its allowance; George Russell's five-place penalty is separate.
items.why_it_matters: The technical report and penalty decisions are distinct. Qualifying and the regulation determine the final grid allocation for the 30-place penalties; Perez's separate Document 40 formal warning is not another grid drop.

sources.label: FIA: Technical Delegate's new-element report, Document 30
FIA: Russell's separate five-place decision, Document 15

items.title: Perez receives a formal warning after discarding a loose cockpit item
items.summary: FIA Document 40 resolves the FP3 unsafe-condition summons in Document 31. After reviewing in-car video, the Stewards found that Perez threw a small plastic cable organiser, which had detached from the seat belt, out of the car. Cadillac received a formal warning: throwing material onto the track during a live session was inappropriate even though this small, light item was unlikely to damage another car or injure a driver.
items.why_it_matters: The warning follows a safety-related finding, but is not a grid penalty. Keep it separate from Perez's 30-place power-unit sanction in Document 39.

sources.label: FIA: decision and formal warning, Document 40
FIA: resolved Sergio Perez summons, Document 31

items.title: Mercedes can clinch the constructors' title with a three-point gain
items.summary: The latest official standings show Mercedes on 630 points, 126 ahead of Ferrari on 504. Formula1.com's pre-weekend scenario says Mercedes clinches the constructors' title if it gains three points on Ferrari in Brazil; the practice sessions have not changed the standings.
items.why_it_matters: The Drivers' title is already settled, but the teams' championship remains live. Practice awards no points, so the three-point threshold is still a race-weekend scenario.

items.title: FIA outlines post-Qualifying weighing and interview sequence
items.summary: The FIA Media Delegate's Document 29 sets the post-Qualifying route for the top three, FIA weighing in race gear, Parc Fermé interviews, and press-conference/TV-pen duties. Other drivers have immediate weighing and media requirements after their final qualifying part; the document includes a Parc Fermé layout.
items.why_it_matters: These are post-session operational instructions, not a change to the qualifying classification or a grid penalty.

sources.label: FIA: Parc Fermé layout, Document 29 page 4
